scenes.narration: In 1206, one engineer described a machine you could program.
scenes.prompt: A dim 13th-century stone workshop at night, oil lamps glowing, an engineer seen from behind leaning over a large brass and wood clockwork machine with turning gears, slow dolly-in over his shoulder.

scenes.label: Upper Mesopotamia · 1206
scenes.narration: His name was Al-Jazari, chief engineer at the Artuqid court in Upper Mesopotamia.
scenes.prompt: Golden-hour aerial shot over a medieval Mesopotamian stone citadel on a hill above a river valley, palm trees and mudbrick houses, slow drone push forward.

scenes.narration: His name was Al-Jazari, chief engineer at the Artuqid court in Upper Mesopotamia.

scenes.label: The Book of Knowledge
scenes.narration: That year he finished The Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices.
scenes.prompt: Close-up of a scholar's hands turning the pages of an old illuminated manuscript full of hand-drawn machine diagrams, candlelight flicker, slow tilt across the page.

scenes.title: The programmable drum machine
scenes.narration: One was a band of musical automata. Pegs on a rotating drum set the beat. Move the pegs, change the rhythm.

scenes.label: Still turning today
scenes.narration: The crankshaft and camshaft he described still turn inside engines today.
scenes.prompt: Macro shot inside a modern car engine, polished crankshaft and camshaft spinning in warm light, slow orbit around the metal parts.
